{
  "claim": "recover_json_object does not score a fenced JSON object with repeated keys from the fenced pool, so it can select a later top-level object instead of the last fenced object.",
  "expected": "The last fenced object is scored, with repeated keys resolved last-wins. For the reproducer, the recovered object is {\"a\":2}.",
  "observed": "The fenced pool skips the repeated-key object because it only attempts strict JSON, then the top-level pool is used and returns the later top-level object {\"b\":3}.",
  "reproducer": "```json\\n{\\\"a\\\":1,\\\"a\\\":2}\\n```\\n{\\\"b\\\":3}",
  "source_basis": "The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text ... A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Any content with a fenced JSON object containing repeated keys and a later top-level JSON object outside the fence.",
  "uncertainty": ""
}
